conflict_topics: Allocation of weeknight cooking/cleaning slots (fairness of rota)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants provide concrete proposals (wash rule, weeknight rota) and specific justifications (A: 'I cook most nights'; D: 'I usually get home late').
Key rules and requests are repeated several times ('whoever uses the shared pan, wash it straight after'), causing moderate repetition.
Dialogue stays consistent with setting details (extractor, kitchen door, group chat) and roles (who cooks when).
Some role friction: A repeatedly frames a fairness claim about slots without others' explicit agreement, which sustains the unresolved tension.
evaluation.final_reason: The immediate practical conflict over the dirty pan and smell was addressed when Agent A agreed to wipe and wash the pan and turn on the extractor and close the door ('Okay — I'll wipe and wash the pan now, turn on the extractor and close the door.' — Round 3). Agent D also posted preferred weeknights ('Tuesday and Thursday' — Round 5). However, the substantive allocation dispute over who should receive 'extra' rota slots remains unresolved because Agent A repeatedly insisted they 'shouldn't be given extra slots' ('I cook most nights, so don't give me extra slots.' — Rounds 2, 3, 6) and the other housemates have not accepted or negotiated that claim; the weeknight rota has not been finalised for all members (B has not posted).
position_change_notes: Agent A changed position on the immediate cleanliness demand: initially defensive about slots but in Round 3 explicitly agreed to wipe and wash the pan and run the extractor ('I'll wipe and wash the pan now, turn on the extractor and close the door').
Agent D consistently requested later slots and followed through by posting preferred weeknights (Tuesday and Thursday).
Agent B consistently prioritized immediate mitigation for sleep/work (asked for extractor and door closed) and deferred rota details to tomorrow.
Agent C consistently pushed for clear cleaning rules and use of the group chat to finalise rota; C's position is stable throughout.

round_scores.evidence: Agent C: 'Who used the shared pan last night? Can we agree that whoever uses the shared pan washes it straight after?...let's do a simple weekend rota' — Agent D: 'rota sounds fair. Can we do simple weeknight slots...I usually get home late — can I take a later slot?' (Complaint about pan + proposals for rules and slot preference introduced; no agreement yet.)

Agent A: 'Rota sounds fine. Agent D, take a later weeknight slot. But whoever uses the shared pan must wash it straight after...I cook most nights, so I shouldn't be given extra slots.' — Agent B: 'Agent A, please wipe and wash the pan now — the smell's already in the corridor and I need to sleep early for work. Can you also turn the extractor on and close the kitchen door?' (Direct demands and a contested allocation claim create clear disagreement.)

Agent A: 'Okay — I'll wipe and wash the pan now, turn on the extractor and close the door. But we need to stick to the rule: whoever uses the shared pan washes it straight after; I cook most nights, so don't give me extra slots.' — Agent B: 'Agent A, please wipe and wash the pan now and turn the extractor on. Close the kitchen door — I need to sleep early. We can sort the rota tomorrow.' (Immediate cleanliness is accepted and about to be addressed, reducing acute conflict; allocation dispute remains.)

Agent C: 'Agent A, please wash the pan now and turn the extractor on. Let's agree the weeknight rota tomorrow evening in the group chat.' — Agent D: 'Okay, sounds fair. I'll pick two later weeknights in the group chat.' (Participants move toward agreeing process for rota; immediate issue appears to be handled.)

Agent C: 'Agent D, please post your two weeknights in the group chat tonight. Everyone else, pick two nights too. Reminder: whoever uses the shared pan, wash it straight after and wipe out the fat.' — Agent D: 'Okay. I'll post my two later weeknights in the group chat now: Tuesday and Thursday.' (One housemate posts slots; rota still incomplete but process is progressing.)

Agent C: 'Agent A, Agent B: please post your two weeknights now so we can finalise the rota.' — Agent A: 'I'll take Monday and Friday. Whoever uses the shared pan must wash it straight after — I cook most nights, so don't give me extra slots.' (A reasserts a contested allocation claim; rota remains unfinalised and the fairness question persists.)

substantive_insights: Two distinct issues: (1) an acute operational problem (dirty pan/smell) and (2) a distributive fairness problem (assignment of weeknight slots). The acute issue was admitted and addressed; the distributive issue remains.
Arrival times and work patterns drive incompatible constraints: D requests later slots due to late arrival; A cites frequent cooking and resists extra slots.
Process-oriented solution (use group chat to pick nights) is adopted, which moves the group toward formalising duties but has not yet produced full mutual agreement.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 3 because the final status is partially_resolved.
